original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose an exact caller and a new demand/interface hypothesis. Read the scoped #5617/#5631/#5649/#5747 and #5720/#5745 objections before rebuilding an excluded schedule. Compare the complete matched source/consumer protocols including all retained helper outputs. For an active-mode injection, first check #5745: its canonical delivery claim repays the eight removed centre jobs. Audit that exact claim or change its channel/feedback hypothesis; do not repeat the same free-injection search. Stop if the full favorable budget fails or the required restored output is unobservable.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.

actual_scope: Decide three-versus-four dyadic cube queries for PR6200's fixed cubic reader in PR6653's integer-shift alphabet (integer a += k*b only, queries on a only) at every odd-S arity 3 <= r <= 200, and certify twenty further arities with three general-frame queries (PR6212/PR7475 contract); retain all r children and restore arbitrary dirty sources.
scope_change_reason: A bounded coefficient/restoration side question of the joint-query-controller card, continuing PR6653 Open next question 1 and PR7479 Open next question 2, not the card's complete physical supplier acceptance gate. Changes the alphabet relative to the card: the obstruction is proved only for integer shifts on a, the certificates use general frames.
bottleneck_link: Side result: closes the integer-direction route at 82 odd-S arities (so any three-query repair there must use b or non-integer shifts) and adds twenty exact three-query arities. Physical prices and caller overhead remain unknown; no supplier or kappa change.
stop_rule: Stop after the complete odd-S integer-shift classification to r=200, explicit four-query witnesses, twenty independently replayed general-frame programs and two separate exact checkers; do not extend to physical savings without a matched bill.
evidence: PROOF.md: Lemmas 0-5 and Theorems A-B. CERTIFICATES.json: 34 integer node sets, 17 three-query and 82 four-query integer-shift programs, 20 general-frame programs. verify.py (complete d-route search, exact elimination, symbolic execution, source pins, nine controls) and independent_check.py (y-route search with Cipolla roots, six-point identities, separate interpreter, five controls), each normal and under -O; build.py --check regenerates the certificates byte for byte.

ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance: certificate search, proofs, both checkers and the generator were produced with AI agents (including Anthropic Claude); the two checkers are separate implementations. No independent human or formal proof-kernel review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Do the 38 open odd-S arities r <= 200 (first 15, 22, 30, 31) admit three dyadic queries in general frames?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the remaining three-versus-four question; Theorem A shows a repair must read or write b or use non-integer shifts.
open_questions.first_step: Extend the parity Lemma 3 to primitive rows with even u (dyadic shifts) and combine with PR7506's height-64 bound at r=15.
open_questions.blocked_by: With non-monic rows the weight made integral in Lemma 4 need not be integral, so no size bound is known.

open_questions.question: Do the even-S arities 40, 61, 141, 165, 168, 193, 196 admit three dyadic queries?
open_questions.why_it_matters: They are the only even-S arities r <= 200 still open after this package.
open_questions.first_step: Search two non-monic rows with the third row forced by the node equation, or test local solvability of the squareness condition; a local unpackaged search with two integer nodes |c| <= 12000 found none.
open_questions.blocked_by: For even S there is no parity lemma and hence no finite reduction.

open_questions.question: Do the cheapest new programs (four shears at 124, 169, 177, 184; six at 57, 120, 192) beat r eager restoration shears?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Query-count minima only matter if the complete event bill is smaller.
open_questions.first_step: Price their weighted queries and shears under one pinned backend using PR7475's event inequality.
open_questions.blocked_by: Unpriced coefficient preparation, precision, routing, storage and caller work.

family_decision.boundary: Fixed cubic reader, all r children retained, arbitrary dirty sources restored exactly, no output feedback; integer-shift alphabet for Theorem A, PR6212 general frames for Theorem B; 3 <= r <= 200.
family_decision.evidence_status: author-checked with two separate AI-assisted implementations
family_decision.stop: No further arity census until the parity lemma is extended to non-monic rows or a priced comparison is requested.
